Cautiously optimistic, with a modest upward tilt once the Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey (SLOOS) is incorporated. The FOMC’s June 2021 stance remains highly accommodative (near‑zero policy rate, ongoing Treasury/MBS purchases, and average‑inflation framework), and the May 2021 FSR still flags vulnerabilities (elevated valuations, some market‑structure fragilities, elevated business leverage, stress in parts of CRE). However, SLOOS suggests credit supply is healing:

- Banks report easing standards for residential real estate (including GSE-eligible mortgages) and HELOCs, and across consumer credit (credit card, auto, and other consumer), including reduced minimum credit-score thresholds, even as standards remain tighter than pre‑pandemic in some categories.
- For firms, standards have eased for investment‑grade borrowers, while foreign banks kept IG largely unchanged but tightened for below‑investment‑grade; some large banks still show pockets of C&I policy tightness.
- CRE underwriting remains cautious in segments like nonfarm nonresidential and construction/development.

Net: Broader credit availability to households and IG corporates offsets some of the FSR caution, while riskier borrowers and CRE remain constrained. This nudges the tone from moderately positive to somewhat more constructive.
